reason: E2 directly supports radiation-induced Cr/V precipitation and negligible hardening in the nanocrystalline alloy, and E1 supports the role of grain boundaries as defect sinks. However, no cited evidence supports the claims that coarsening reduces segregation driving forces or that SPS can achieve this without thermal precipitation.
premises: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits radiation-induced Cr/V-rich precipitation
The alloy shows negligible irradiation hardening up to 8 dpa
Grain boundaries act as defect sinks that annihilate irradiation-induced defects
Coarsening grains to an ultrafine scale reduces chemical potential gradients driving Cr/V segregation
Spark plasma sintering can coarsen grains without triggering thermal precipitation
